name: Krebs Cycle Causal Benchmark
description: Learning causal relationships between a set of variables is a challenging problem in computer science. Many existing artificial benchmark datasets are based on sampling from causal models and thus contain residual information that the ${R} ^2$-sortability can identify. Here, we present a benchmark for methods in causal learning using time series. The presented dataset is not ${R}^2$-sortable and is based on a real-world scenario of the Krebs cycle that is used in cells to release energy. We provide four scenarios of learning, including short and long time series, and provide guidance so that testing is unified between possible users.
evaluation_method: Structural Hamming Distance (SHD), precision/recall and F1 on recovered edges
reputation: Niche benchmark in causal-discovery for time-series with biological realism; limited adoption so far.
notes: Small, domain-specific real-world time-series dataset (four scenarios); intentionally non-R^2-sortable; results sensitive to preprocessing and algorithmic assumptions; not an LLM benchmark.
